title: Lawyering skills: interviewing, counseling, negotiation and trial advocacy
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Interview and counsel clients, investigate facts, negotiate and mediate, and try a case (openings, direct and cross-examination, exhibits, objections and closings), building the practical skills the NextGen bar exam tests.
primary_reading: NCBE: the NextGen bar exam and its foundational skills

blocks.deliverable: Plan and script a client interview for a supplied problem.
Write a counseling letter that lays out options and risks.
Prepare a negotiation plan with a BATNA and a reservation point.
Week 7 midterm; outline a settlement agreement.
Write a direct and a cross-examination of a supplied witness.
Prepare a closing argument from a supplied trial record.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Mock case: from a supplied case file, prepare a trial notebook (case theory, opening, two direct and two cross-examinations, exhibit foundations and a closing) and a negotiation plan for settlement.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
